items.stableKey: p47:figure:Figure 2.2 CUDA organizes parallel execution into a two-level hierarchy. Threads
items.title: Figure 2.2 CUDA organizes parallel execution into a two-level hierarchy. Threads are the smallest unit of execution and are grouped into blocks. Blocks are then organized into a grid. Each thread has a unique ID within its block ( threadIdx ), and each block has a unique ID within the grid ( blockIdx ). Combined with the block size ( blockDim ), these indices let every thread compute a globally unique position to process.

items.stableKey: p49:figure:Figure 2.3 When the total number of elements is not evenly divisible by the bloc
items.title: Figure 2.3 When the total number of elements is not evenly divisible by the block size, CUDA launches extra threads beyond the valid data range. The shaded region shows threads whose computed index exceeds the array bounds. Each thread must check whether its index is valid before accessing memory; threads outside the bounds simply return early without doing any work. This boundary check prevents illegal memory accesses that would otherwise crash the program or corrupt data.

items.stableKey: p52:figure:Figure 2.4 For 3D data, such as volumetric images or batched 2D tensors, CUDA su
items.title: Figure 2.4 For 3D data, such as volumetric images or batched 2D tensors, CUDA supports 3D grids of 3D blocks. Each thread identifies its position using six built-in variables: blockIdx in x, y, and z for the block’s position in the grid, and threadIdx in x, y, and z for the thread’s position within its block. The total number of threads per block (x times y times z) must not exceed 1,024 on most GPUs.

items.stableKey: p237:figure:Figure 8.2 Flash Attention loads small tiles of Q , K , and V from HBM into fast
items.title: Figure 8.2 Flash Attention loads small tiles of Q , K , and V from HBM into fast on-chip SRAM. All intermediate results (the score matrix S and probability matrix P ) stay in SRAM and are never written to HBM. Only the final output O is written back.

items.stableKey: p238:figure:Figure 8.3 Online softmax streams one query row’s scores tile by tile. Each step
items.title: Figure 8.3 Online softmax streams one query row’s scores tile by tile. Each step keeps only the current tile in SRAM plus three running values: the max m , the denominator l , and the output O . When a new tile raises the max, the old l and O are rescaled by exp(m_old - m_new) , so the final O / l equals the exact full-row softmax result.
